original_question: Let B be a C-semi-greedy basis in a quasi-Banach space. Does there always exist an equivalent renorming of the space under which B becomes 1-semi-greedy?
target_in_paper: Section 4.1, Question 5: "If B is C-semi-greedy in a quasi-Banach space, is there a renorming such that the basis is 1-semi-greedy?"
correct_elements: Your draft has already identified the right open problem very closely: it asks about a C-semi-greedy basis in a quasi-Banach space and whether one can pass to an equivalent renorming that makes the same basis 1-semi-greedy. That is exactly the renorming question posed in Section 4.1 of the paper.
missing_details: In the paper, semi-greediness is formulated for a Markushevich basis B=(x_n,x_n^*) in a quasi-Banach space X; the paper also globally assumes such bases are semi-normalized.
The exact definition of C-semi-greedy should be stated: for every x in X and every finite greedy set A of x, one has min{||x-Σ_{n∈A} a_n x_n|| : a_n in F} ≤ C_sg σ_|A|(x).
The best m-term approximation error σ_m(x) should be spelled out: σ_m(x)=inf{||x-Σ_{n∈E} b_n x_n|| : E subset of N, |E|≤m, b_n in F}.
The meaning of a greedy set A of x should be made explicit: if |A|=m, then min_{n∈A}|x_n^*(x)| ≥ max_{n∉A}|x_n^*(x)|.
The ambient scalar field should be specified as F = R or C, since that is how quasi-Banach spaces are set up in the paper.
The renorming should be identified as an equivalent quasi-norm ||·||' on the same underlying space X, with ||tx||' = |t| ||x||' and ||x||' approximately equivalent to ||x||.

It should be made explicit that the same basis B is required to become 1-semi-greedy with respect to the new quasi-norm, and that the paper does not add extra Schauder, bi-monotone, Banach, or p-Banach hypotheses to this renorming question.
refined_question: Let X be a quasi-Banach space over F in {R,C}, and let B=(x_n,x_n^*)_{n in N} be a semi-normalized Markushevich basis of X. Assume that B is C_sg-semi-greedy, meaning that for every x in X and every finite greedy set A subset of N of x (that is, if |A|=m then min_{n in A}|x_n^*(x)| >= max_{n not in A}|x_n^*(x)|), one has min{||x-Σ_{n in A} a_n x_n|| : a_n in F} <= C_sg sigma_m(x), where sigma_m(x):=inf{||x-Σ_{n in E} b_n x_n|| : E subset of N, |E|<=m, b_n in F}. Does there exist an equivalent quasi-norm ||·||' on X (equivalently, a renorming with ||tx||' = |t| ||x||' and ||x||' approximately equivalent to ||x|| for all t in F and x in X) such that the same basis B is 1-semi-greedy in (X,||·||')?
justification: The draft is targeting the renorming problem that appears after the paper discusses the isometric case of semi-greediness and existing renorming results for quasi-greedy, almost-greedy, greedy, and partially-greedy bases. The exact official formulation is Section 4.1, Question 5 on page 18. To make the question stand-alone and faithful to the paper, one must import the paper's definitions of greedy set and greedy sum from the Thresholding Greedy Algorithm setup in Section 4, the best m-term error sigma_m from the greediness discussion, the exact semi-greedy inequality from Definition 4.14, and the paper's quasi-Banach notion of renorming from Lemma 4.22. The nearby Theorem 4.17 and Theorem 4.20 explain why semi-greediness and the constant 1 are being discussed here, but they do not give an equivalent reformulation of Question 5 itself.
